data.title: The Silent Choir, Keeper of Unspoken Truths
Final Note: The Patrons Do Not Care
The Clockwork Monad, the Iterative Forge
Temporary Anima of the Clockwork Monad
Aveh, the Rider Behind the Storm
Grimmir, the Old Man of the Forest
The Sacred Geometry, Architect of Perfect Forms
Morag the Hag, Weaver of Hidden Costs
The Breath of the First Forge, the Spark in the Maker's Hand
Temporary Anima of the First Forge
Hidden Pavilion --- An archive behind a curtain of falling water.
data.body: The water muffles sound. Secrets spoken here cannot be overheard --- but the water remembers.

data.title: Chamber of the Ninth Scroll --- A locked room with a single blank scroll on a pedestal.
data.body: The scroll is not blank. It is written in disappearing ink. The reagent is moonlight.

data.title: Well of Forgotten Names --- A stone well where the Lethai-thora throw scrolls that are too dangerous to keep.
data.body: The well is bottomless. The scrolls burn as they fall. The smoke forms faces.

data.title: Ink-Maker's Studio --- A cave with grinding stones and jars of pigment.
data.body: The ink is made from crushed beetles, iron ore, and tears. The tears are the ink-maker's own.

data.title: Silent Scriptorium --- A hall where scribes copy scrolls without speaking.
data.body: They write with their left hands. Their right hands are for swearing oaths.

data.title: Context Key Archive --- A vault of stones, each carved with a season and a place.
data.body: A scroll cannot be read without the correct context key. The keys are scattered across Sihai.

data.title: Emperor's Censorate --- A building near the archive, staffed by imperial spies.
data.body: They pretend not to know about the hidden pavilion. The Lethai-thora pretend not to notice them.

data.title: Bridge of Unspoken Names --- A stone arch where the Lethai-thora whisper secrets to the river.
data.body: The river carries the secrets to the sea. The sea does not tell.

data.title: Shrine of the Silent Gods --- A ruined temple where the old fey beings were once worshipped.
data.body: The gods are not dead. They are waiting. The Lethai-thora leave offerings of ink. [J] The Forgotten Ledger's Vault --- A subterranean room with a single iron door. The door has nine locks. The keys are held by nine different keepers. The ninth keeper is dead. [Q] Memory-Thread Chamber --- A room where Lethai-thora weave their hair into cords. Each thread contains a memory. Cutting a thread releases the memory --- and kills the keeper. [K] The Emperor's Secret Archive (Hidden) --- A duplicate archive built by a paranoid emperor. It contains the same scrolls as the Lethai-thora's, plus the emperor's own confessions. [A] The First Pavilion (Myth) --- Where the first Lethai-thora hid the first forbidden scroll. It is said to be invisible. Only those who have forgotten nine names can see it. enumerate

data.title: Keeper of the Seventh Gutter --- Old, silent, writing on water with a reed brush.
data.body: ``The words vanish,'' she says. ``That is how I know they are true.''

data.title: Scroll-Binder --- A man with no shadow. He lost it to a scroll that ate his reflection.
data.body: He ties silk cords around each scroll. The knots are the secrets.

data.title: Ink-Maker --- A woman with stained hands and a jar of moonstone ink.
data.body: ``This ink only writes during an eclipse,'' she says. ``The next eclipse is in nine days.''

data.title: Quiet Chancellor --- An imperial censor in gray robes. He speaks in couplets.
data.body: The first couplet is a greeting. The second is a threat. The third is a bribe.

data.title: Memory-Weaver --- A woman with a loom made of human hair. She weaves memories into cloth.
data.body: The cloth is soft. It whispers the memory when you touch it.

data.title: Imperial Spy --- A young man posing as a scribe. He has a hidden seal.
data.body: He is looking for a scroll that names the emperor's true father. He will pay.

data.title: Ghost of the Ninth Scroll --- A blank scroll that floats through the archive at midnight.
data.body: It weeps ink. The ink forms words. The words are a secret that killed its keeper.

data.title: Forbidden Scholar --- A monk who was excommunicated for reading a scroll he should not have.
data.body: His eyes are gone. He reads by touch. The scrolls burn his fingers.

data.title: Silent Guard --- A warrior who took a vow of silence to protect the archive. He communicates by writing on his own skin. His skin is full of scars. The First Keeper --- A translucent figure in scholar's robes, seen at the well. She asks
data.body: ``What secret do you wish to forget?'' The answer becomes a scroll. [Q] The Censorate's Interrogator --- A man with a brass scale. He weighs truth and lies. His scale is balanced. He has never found a truth heavy enough. [K] The Emperor's Dreamer --- A woman who dreams the emperor's nightmares. She knows what he fears. She is kept in a locked room. The Lethai-thora want to free her. [A] The Forgotten God's Echo --- A voice from the ruined shrine. It speaks in a language no one understands. The Lethai-thora say it is the last fey being. It is asking for a memory. enumerate

data.title: Forged Scroll --- A tax ledger is discovered to be a fake. The forgery is perfect.
data.body: The forger is a Lethai-thora. The scroll is not a forgery --- it is the original. The empire's copy is wrong.

data.title: Missing Context Key --- A scroll cannot be read without a specific stone. The stone is lost.
data.body: The stone was stolen by the Censorate. They want to destroy the scroll.

data.title: Witness Demanded --- The Quiet Chancellor asks the party to witness a secret exchange.
data.body: If they agree, they become bound by the Lethai-thora's silence. If they refuse, they are exiled from the archive.

data.title: Archive Fire --- A lamp falls. Scrolls burn. The smoke forms names.
data.body: The names are those of the keepers. One is yours.

data.title: Censorate Raid --- Imperial inspectors arrive with a warrant. They have a list of forbidden scrolls.
data.body: The list is accurate. Someone inside the archive is a spy.

data.title: Memory-Thread Cut --- A keeper's memory-thread is severed. She forgets everything.
data.body: The thread was cut by an assassin. The assassin wants a secret only she knew.

data.title: Silence Broken --- A keeper speaks aloud for the first time in decades. The Hollow hears. The Hollow sends an Oath-Keeper. The Oath-Keeper asks
data.body: ``What did you say?''

data.title: Ink of Truth --- Someone poisons the ink well. Writing with it forces you to confess.
data.body: The poison was placed by the Censorate. They want to know where the forbidden scroll is.

data.title: Emperor's Death --- The emperor dies. The Mandate wavers. The archive is vulnerable. The new emperor will burn the scrolls. The Lethai-thora must hide them --- or die. Ghost of the Ninth Scroll Awakens --- The blank scroll fills with ink. The ink is a name. The name is the next person to die. The name is yours. The First Pavilion Appears --- The mythic archive manifests. It is invisible to most. The party can see it. They are now witnesses to a secret that has been hidden for a thousand years. The Hollow will want it. Censorate's Interrogation --- The party is arrested and brought before the brass scale. The interrogator asks one question
data.body: ``What did the Lethai-thora tell you?'' The scale will know if you lie. [A] The Forgotten God Wakes --- The voice from the shrine becomes a scream. The ground shakes. The god wants its memory back. The memory is held in a scroll. The scroll is the Ninth Scroll. enumerate

data.title: Forbidden Scroll --- A scroll sealed with silk cord. It contains one truth no one wants spoken.
data.body: Read it aloud, and the secret becomes known. The speaker will be hunted.

data.title: Context Key Stone --- A carved stone. Unlocks the meaning of one specific scroll.
data.body: The stone is warm. It glows when held near the correct scroll.

data.title: Memory-Thread --- A cord woven from a keeper's hair. Cut it to release a memory.
data.body: The memory is a secret. The keeper will forget it. The cutter will remember it.

data.title: Ink-Stone --- A jar of ink made from crushed moonstones. Writes only during eclipses.
data.body: The ink reveals truths that cannot be spoken. Use it to write a secret that will last.

data.title: Silence Token --- A small brass charm. Present it to demand a moment of silence in any court.
data.body: During the silence, no one can lie. The truth will echo.

data.title: Keeper's Lamp --- A brass lamp that never goes out. The flame flickers when a lie is spoken nearby.
data.body: The lamp also flickers when a secret is hidden in the room.

data.title: Quiet Chancellor's Seal --- A jade seal. Press it to any document to grant it imperial immunity from censorship.
data.body: The seal is a forgery. The Chancellor made it himself. It still works.

data.title: Scroll of Forgotten Names --- A scroll that lists the names of everyone who has been erased from history.
data.body: Speak a name, and that person's deeds become known. The Hollow will remember them too.

data.title: Ink-Maker's Grinding Stone --- A stone bowl. Grind any pigment into ink that writes the truth.
data.body: The truth cannot be erased. The ink will burn through lies. [J] Ghost's Tear (Vial) --- A vial of ink wept by the Ghost of the Ninth Scroll. Write a name with it, and that person will forget one secret. The secret is your choice. [Q] First Pavilion's Key (Invisible) --- An invisible key that opens the mythic archive. You cannot see the key. You can feel it. It is cold. [K] Emperor's Nightmare (Scroll) --- A scroll containing the emperor's most feared secret. Read it aloud to make the emperor confess --- or to drive him mad. [A] Forgotten God's Memory (Glass Shard) --- A piece of green glass that hums. It contains a fragment of a fey god's memory. Once, touch it to learn a secret of the old world. The secret will cost a memory of equal weight. enumerate

data.title: Broken Milestone 2 \ On the old Imperial Road; borders ``moved'' overnight. \ The stone has been chiseled seven times. The last mark is still wet. The first was cut by Utaran legionaries. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: If you camp here, roll Spirit + Lore (DV 4). On success, you learn the true border line (+1 die on navigation for this leg). On failure, the milestone moves while you sleep --- start a Lost Ways [4] timer.

data.title: Vine-Terrace Hillside 3 \ Abandoned press; strangler ivy owns it now. \ The ivy has grown around a skeleton. The skeleton still holds a wine cup. The vintage was the year the last governor left. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Foraging here gives 1 Supply, but the ivy is possessive. On a Miss, you are entangled (Body+Athletics DV 3 to break free) and tick Curse Awakening +1.

data.title: Toll-Bridge Town 4 \ Over a cold river; two tolls, no receipts. \ The second toll is collected by a child. The child does not speak. The bridge was built by the legions. It remembers their footsteps. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Crossing costs 1 Boon or 1 Supply. If you refuse, the child writes your name in chalk. The bridge will demand double next time.

data.title: Wolfstairs Pass 5 \ Switchbacks beneath a stonefall cliff. \ The stones were placed by a landslide that knew your name. The pass was the empire's eastern gate. No army has crossed it in a century. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Navigation DV +2. On a Partial, you are spotted by a free company scout --- start Rival Hunt [4].

data.title: Sootfall Abbey Ruins 6 \ Bell tower intact; crypts breathing. \ The breathing is a prayer. The monks are still down there. They have been praying for the empire's soul for two hundred years. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: A character who prays with the monks (Spirit+Lore DV 3) clears 1 Fatigue, but the monks ask for a story about a broken promise. Refusal ticks Curse Awakening +1.

data.title: Hill-Motte 7 \ Fresh palisade; ditch scattered with caltrops. \ The caltrops are from a siege that ended last week. The bodies are still rotting. The siege was over a bridge toll. The bridge has not collected in fifty years. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: The lord of the motte will hire the party as mercenaries (1 Supply). If they refuse, he accuses them of being spies --- start Feud Spark [4].

data.title: Border-Stone Ring 8 \ Carved with seven crowns; each points wrong. \ The crowns belong to kings who never existed. The stones remember them anyway. The eighth crown was the empire's. It is not carved. It is implied. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: A character who touches the eighth (empty) crown must test Resolve (DV 4). On failure, they gain the Condition Marked by the Curse (GM may spend 1 SB to worsen Position in any negotiation).

data.title: Blackwood Charcoalers' Hollow 9 \ Witch-posts at every path. \ The witch-posts were made from the gibbets of tax collectors. The tax collectors still swing. They were collecting for the empire. They have not stopped. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: A hedge-witch offers to read your fortune (1 Boon). On a success, she warns of the next Curse Stirrs trigger. On a failure, she demands a memory (erase a minor fact).

data.title: Salt-Road Ford 10 \ Rains expose old bones in the chalk banks. \ The bones are from three wars. They are not all human. The ford was the empire's salt route. The salt is still in the water. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Crossing costs 1 Fatigue (cold). If you drink the water, test Endurance DV 3. On failure, you see the ghosts of the drowned for the next scene (--1 die on all actions).

data.title: Iron Mine Adits J \ Held by a miners' commune; the air is full of whispers. \ The whispers are the mine's memory. It remembers every collapse. The last collapse was the year the empire fell. The miners are still digging. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: The commune will trade 1 Supply for a miner's story. If the story is true, they also reveal a hidden exit --- treat the next travel timer as 2 segments shorter.

data.title: Margravine's Hunting Lodge Q \ Tapestries of victories that never were. \ The tapestries were woven by a blind weaver. The threads are from her own hair. The victories are Utaran. The weaver was Acasian. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: A character who studies the tapestries (Wits+Lore DV 4) learns a noble's secret (a String). On a failure, the blind weaver's ghost asks for a favor --- start Weaver's Debt [4].

data.title: War-Camp City K \ Tents around a burned keep; every banner claims the throne. \ The keep was burned by its own lord. He did not want to share the heat. The lord was the last imperial governor. He died in the fire. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: To enter the camp, you must swear a temporary oath to a claimant. Breaking it ticks Curse Awakening +2.

data.title: The Pale Causeway A \ The last high road that survives the spring thaws. \ The causeway is made of bones. The bones are from the workers who built it. The workers were Acasian. The empire paid them in promises. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Crossing the Causeway at dusk forces a Resolve test (DV 4). On failure, you gain the Condition Debtor to the Dead (any spirit can demand one service from you). On a critical failure, the Curse Awakening timer ticks +2 immediately. enumerate

data.title: Tithe-Collector's Runner 2 \ Tally-rod, empty stomach, and a list of names. \ His tally-rod has notches from a dozen villages. The villages are now empty. He collects for the Margravine. She does not ask where the grain goes. \ Debt they owe
data.body: He owes his soul to the Margravine's ledger. If you give him a name from the list, he will mark it paid --- but the ghost of that name will haunt you. \ Price of aid: 1 Supply or a story about a tax collector who died hungry.

data.title: Roadside Prior 3 \ Three lay brothers guarding a relic. \ The relic is a finger bone. The prior claims it belonged to a saint who starved to death. The saint was an Utaran missionary. The Acasians ate his offerings. \ Debt they owe
data.body: The prior's order swore to feed the poor. They have failed. He will help anyone who shares a meal. \ Price of aid: A crust of bread and a prayer. If you refuse, the relic's ghost will follow you (--1 die on all stealth rolls for one scene).

data.title: Hedge-Witch 4 \ Knows which bridges eat travelers. \ Her price is a story. The story must have a bad ending. She has heard all the good ones. The bridges listen when she speaks. \ Debt they owe
data.body: She once cursed a tax collector. The curse still echoes. If you help her lift it, she will teach you a route that ignores the Curse once. \ Price of aid: A story that ends with a death. If the story is true, she gives you a Salt Ward (Diamond). If false, the bridges will remember you.

data.title: Free Company Captain 5 \ Pike and shot between contracts. \ He has served three kings this year. He does not remember their names. His first contract was with a man who called himself emperor. The man is dead. The contract is not. \ Debt they owe
data.body: He owes back pay to his company. If you pay 1 Supply, he will fight for you for one scene. \ Price of aid: A contract signed in blood. If you break it, the Curse Awakening ticks +2.

data.title: River Reeve 6 \ Rents every boat twice. \ His paper is a single page folded into a boat. The other half is elsewhere. The other half is in the Margravine's counting house. She does not know. \ Debt they owe
data.body: He stole the half-page from the Margravine. If you return it, he will waive all tolls for a season. \ Price of aid: A bribe of 1 Boon or a secret about the river. He will also betray you for a better offer.

data.title: Salt-Baron 7 \ Hired blades; owns the ford and your timetable. \ His salt is gray. It was cut with ashes from a burned village. The village refused to pay the imperial salt tax. The empire is dead. The salt is not. \ Debt they owe
data.body: He took a loan from the Margravine's counting house. If you pay it (2 Supply), he will give you a Salt Charter (pass any ford free). \ Price of aid: A wagon of gray salt. Using it in a bargain gives +1 die to intimidation, but the ghost of the burned village will haunt the transaction.

data.title: Blackwood Matriarch 8 \ Tends the feud like a garden. \ Her garden grows tombstones. She waters them with tears---her enemies'. Her grandmother was the last Acasian to hold an imperial title. The empire took it back. She has not forgotten. \ Debt they owe
data.body: The empire stole her grandmother's title. If you recover the original charter (in the Sealed Dowry Chest), she will name you her heir. \ Price of aid: A lock of hair from a blood enemy. She will not say whose.

data.title: Ex-Imperial Surveyor 9 \ Has the last accurate map. \ The map shows villages that no longer exist. The surveyor visits them anyway. She leaves offerings of bread and ink. The ghosts do not eat. They watch. \ Debt they owe
data.body: She lost the map's key --- a brass compass. Find it, and she will draw you a route that ignores the Curse for one journey. \ Price of aid: A true name of a dead village. She will trade a secret for it.

data.title: ``King'' of Three Villages 10 \ Iron-nail crown, iron-will taxes. \ His crown was a plowshare. He reversed the curse. The curse reversed back. He does not know. \ Debt they owe
data.body: He borrowed the plowshare from a hedge-witch. The witch wants it back. Return it, and he will grant you a tax waiver. \ Price of aid: A day's labor in his fields. If you refuse, he accuses you of oath-breaking --- start a Feud Spark [4].

data.title: Bride with No Dowry but a Claim J \ Daggers in the wedding chest. \ The claim is to a bridge that drowned. The bride intends to collect. The bridge was built by the legions. The legions are gone. The bridge is not. \ Debt they owe
data.body: Her dowry was the bridge's toll. The Margravine seized it. If you help her collect, she will give you a Bridge Token (Diamond). \ Price of aid: A dagger from her chest. Using it in a duel gives +1 die, but the bridge's ghost will claim the loser.

data.title: Margravine of the Broken March Q \ Half saint, half tax roll. \ She has never lost a feud. Her tally stick is her sword. Her great-great-grandfather was the last imperial governor's clerk. He stole the seal. She still has it. \ Debt they owe
data.body: She is losing her grip on the province. If you settle a feud for her, she will give you a Blood-Peace Charter (Diamond). \ Price of aid: A signature on her tally stick. Signing binds you to her service until the feud is settled.

data.title: The Lame King K \ Traveling throne; makes law by pointing. \ His throne is a sedan chair carried by debtors. They owe him everything. He owes the Margravine a bridge toll. He has not paid. The bridge remembers. \ Debt they owe
data.body: He cannot pay the toll. If you pay it for him (2 Supply), he will name you his heir for a day --- you may issue one royal decree. \ Price of aid: A ride on his throne. The debtors will carry you, but you will owe them a favor in return.

data.title: The Cursed Child of Silkstrand A \ A rumor more than a person; her laughter ends sieges. \ She is said to be twelve years old. She has been twelve for a century. She was born on the day the last imperial governor died. She does not age. She does not forget. \ Debt they owe
data.body: She is the Curse's accountant. If you find her, she will tell you how many bridges you owe. \ Price of aid: A name you have never spoken. She will write it in her ledger. The Curse will remember it forever. enumerate

data.title: Peat-Fog 2 \ All horns sound like someone calling your name. \ The name is not yours. Answer it, and the fog will take you. The fog is the empire's last breath. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Navigation rolls are Desperate for the scene. On a Miss, a ghostly tax collector appears. It demands a story or a memory. Refusal ticks Curse Awakening +1.

data.title: Sudden Levy 3 \ Every traveler is pressed for a day's service. \ The levy master has a list. Your name is on it---in fresh ink. The list was copied from an imperial tax roll. The roll is two hundred years old. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Pay 1 Supply or serve. Serving forces a Resolve test (DV 4). On failure, you gain the Condition Impressed (--1 die to all actions until you escape). Start a Levy Escape [4] timer.

data.title: Bridge Feud 4 \ Rival banners drop the chain on your cart. \ The chain was forged from a broken oath. It rattles when liars approach. The oath was sworn to the emperor. The emperor is dead. The chain does not care. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: The chain will only lift if you swear an oath to one of the feuding parties. Swearing ticks Curse Awakening +1 (oaths made on bridges always compound). Refusing forces a fight --- treat as a Cap 2 adversary.

data.title: Grain Blight 5 \ Doubles the tithe; refusal means torches at night. \ The blight has a face. It is the face of a tax collector who died hungry. The collector worked for the empire. The empire did not pay him. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: You may pay double (2 Supply) or refuse. Refusing starts a Village Hunt [4] timer. When full, the villagers attack at night (Cap 3 mob).

data.title: Scree Slide 6 \ Seals the pass; the ``safe'' detour is owned by your enemy. \ The enemy raised the toll yesterday. He was expecting you. The pass was the empire's eastern gate. It still remembers the legions. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Pay 2 Supply to the enemy or find another way. Searching for another way forces a Wits+Lore roll (DV 5). On a failure, you lose 1 segment of progress and gain a Black Mark with the enemy.

data.title: Wedding Turns Ambush 7 \ You are caught between two bloodlines. \ The bride's veil is a shroud. The groom's ring is a knife. The feud began when the empire divided the valley. The valley has not healed. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: You must choose a side or flee. Choosing a side gives you an ally (Cap 2) but starts a Feud Spiral [6] timer with the other. Fleeing costs 1 Fatigue and ticks Curse Awakening +1.

data.title: Witch's Tithe Night 8 \ Lights move in the woods; owe nothing or else. \ The lights have voices. They are arguing over who should collect. They are the ghosts of imperial tax collectors. They have not stopped working. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: The ghosts demand a story. If you cannot tell one, they take 1 of your Boons (or 1 Supply). If you have nothing, they take a memory --- lose 1 XP (refundable by a quest).

data.title: Pox Sign 9 \ On a village gate; your escorts desert you. \ The pox is a rumor. The desertion is real. The pox came with the last imperial supply train. The supply train never arrived. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: You must travel alone for the next leg (no assists). Start a Disease Timer [4]. When full, each PC gains 1 Fatigue.

data.title: Condotta Breaks 10 \ The Free Company flips colors mid-march. \ The new colors are the same as the old colors. The captain just wanted to raise morale. He was hired by the Margravine. He was also hired by the Lame King. He is collecting both salaries. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: The company now fights for your enemy. You may bribe them back (2 Supply) or fight them (Cap 3). Bribing ticks Curse Awakening +1 (broken loyalty compounds).

data.title: Heretic Preacher J \ Sparks a march; toll-gates come down in splinters. \ The preacher's text is a tax receipt. He reads it like scripture. The receipt was issued by the empire. It is still valid. No one knows to whom. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: The preacher will grant you safe passage through the riot if you give him a relic (any Diamond). If you refuse, the mob attacks (Cap 2, and you are separated from allies).

data.title: Imperial Pretender Q \ Arrives; every petty lord changes tabards. \ The pretender's seal is a sunburst. The sunburst is slightly crooked. The seal was stolen from the last governor's tomb. The governor's ghost is following him. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: The pretender offers you a charter (Diamond) if you swear loyalty. Swearing ticks Curse Awakening +2 (the ghost of the governor will remember). Refusing makes him a permanent enemy (start a Pretender's Hunt [6] timer).

data.title: River Overruns the Levee K \ The pontoon goes; your rivals don't. \ The river's name is ``Debt.'' It remembers every unpaid crossing. The empire's engineers built the levees. They calculated the flood levels. They did not calculate the Curse. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: You lose 1 Supply (washed away). If you have no Supply, you lose 1 Boon instead. The GM may also tick Curse Awakening +1 (the river demands interest).

data.title: The Curse Stirrs A \ No matter the road, you return to the same crossroads. \ The crossroads has a signpost. The arms are labeled ``Regret,'' ``Hunger,'' ``The Same.'' The post was planted by the last imperial surveyor. She is still walking. \ Mechanical hook
data.body: Roll on the Curse Stirrs table (see Regional Mood section). The party cannot leave until they pay a toll --- a story, a memory, or a name. enumerate

data.title: Toll-Exemption Plaque 2 \ For one bridge . \ The plaque is a bronze leaf. Hold it up, and the toll-keeper will spit---but step aside. The leaf was minted by the empire. The empire's mines are closed. The metal is still good. \ Curse cost
data.body: Using the plaque ticks Curse Awakening +1 (the bridge will remember your face). If you use it on a bridge that has already taken a toll, the plaque crumbles and the bridge's ghost follows you for a day.

data.title: Monastery Letter 3 \ For bed and bread on a named road. \ The letter is sealed with a wax tear. The monks will honor it---or they will not. The abbot was an imperial clerk. He still follows the old forms. \ Curse cost
data.body: The monks will ask you to pray for the dead. If you refuse, the letter burns and you gain a Black Mark with the monastery. If you pray, clear 1 Fatigue but tick Curse Awakening +1 (the dead listen).

data.title: Wine-Right 4 \ On an abandoned terrace; locals will work for shares. \ The wine is from a vine that grows over a mass grave. It tastes of iron. The grave holds the last imperial garrison. They were paid in promises. \ Curse cost
data.body: Drinking the wine gives +1 die to your next social roll, but the garrison's ghosts will appear in your dreams. The GM gains 1 SB to use on a nightmare complication.

data.title: Condotta Contract 5 \ A signed pike contract . \ The contract is written in blood. The blood is from the captain's own finger. The contract was copied from an imperial legionary oath. The words have changed. The weight has not. \ Curse cost
data.body: If the contract is broken, tick Curse Awakening +2. The captain's ghost will demand a new contract --- signed in your own blood.

data.title: Tithe-Remission Writ 6 \ For a village; they owe you a season's labor. \ The writ is stamped with a bell. The bell's clapper is a finger bone. The bell was cast from melted imperial coinage. The coinage was debased. The bell rings true. \ Curse cost
data.body: Using the writ forces the village to work for you, but the bell's ghost will follow you. Every season, you must offer it a story or lose 1 Boon.

data.title: Border-Stone Adjustment 7 \ Move a line two fields over. \ The adjustment is a lie. The truth is that the line was always there. The line was surveyed by the empire's best geometers. They are all dead. Their measurements are not. \ Curse cost
data.body: The ghost of the surveyor will appear and demand you measure the new line with your own feet. Walk it exactly (8 steps) or lose 1 Fatigue and tick Curse Awakening +1.

data.title: Pass-Key Charm 8 \ Recognized by Pale Causeway watchmen. \ The charm is a knotted cord. Untie it to pass---or to stay. The cord was tied by an imperial courier. The courier's route was swallowed by the Curse. The cord remembers the way. \ Curse cost
data.body: The charm works for one season. After that, the courier's ghost will visit you. He will ask for a message to deliver. If you refuse, the charm becomes a curse --- all roads lead back to the same crossing.

data.title: Sealed Dowry Chest 9 \ Of claims, not coin; certain doors open. \ The chest is locked with a riddle. The answer is a name you do not know. The name is the last imperial governor's. He wrote it on the inside. He is the only one who has seen it. \ Curse cost
data.body: Opening the chest ticks Curse Awakening +3. The governor's ghost will appear and offer a bargain: the name in exchange for a service. Refusing means the chest locks forever.

data.title: Mine-Share 10 \ In the commune; they fight like they mean it. \ The share is a pickaxe. The commune will lend you a miner---or a grave. The mine was opened by the empire's first surveyors. They found iron. They also found something else. They did not name it. \ Curse cost
data.body: The miner will work for you, but the mine's whispers will follow. Once per session, the GM may ask you to name something you found in the dark. If you lie, the miner dies.

data.title: Blood-Peace Charter J \ Suspend a feud long enough to move your wagons. \ The charter is a white ribbon. Blood will not be spilled while it flies---but blood will remember. The ribbon was woven by a hedge-witch. She used thread from a tax collector's uniform. The collector is dead. The thread is not. \ Curse cost
data.body: The truce lasts one scene. After that, the feud returns with interest --- both sides will demand a wergild from you. Pay 2 Supply or start a Double Feud [6].

data.title: Marriage Proxy Q \ From the Margravine; bind a hill-king to your cause. \ The proxy is a wedding veil. The veil was worn by a ghost. The ghost was the Margravine's grandmother. She married an imperial legate. The legate never came home. \ Curse cost
data.body: Using the proxy binds the hill-king to you --- but the ghost will appear at your own wedding (or any celebration). She will ask for a dance. Refusing costs 1 Boon and ticks Curse Awakening +1.

data.title: The Lame King's Traveling Writ K \ Troops must make way . \ The writ is a broken scepter. The Lame King's seal is a footprint. The footprint was pressed into wax by his grandfather. The grandfather was a free company captain. He could not write. He used his boot. \ Curse cost
data.body: The writ works only once. After that, the Lame King will send debtors to collect the scepter. If you refuse, start a King's Hunt [6].

data.title: Curse-Redemption Rite A \ For one night, no crossroads can hold you. \ The rite is a whisper. The whisper is a name you have never spoken. The name is the Curse's. It does not want to be spoken. It does not want to be silent. It wants to be paid. \ Curse cost
data.body: Using the rite clears all Curse Awakening segments for one night. The next morning, the Curse returns with double the segments. You cannot use the rite again in the same province. enumerate

data.title: Salt Pan with Broken Spirit-Cage --- A white flat where the air hums.
data.body: The cage is empty, but it still rattles at night. Something got out. The salt tastes of iron.

data.title: Black Marble Temple --- Steps stained red; the blood never washes away.
data.body: The temple has no windows. The Maeri do not need light. The steps are warm, as if a great beast sleeps beneath.

data.title: The Brass Gate --- A fortified strait with spirit-buoys that scream when crossed.
data.body: Each buoy contains a bound spirit. They sing the names of those who pass. The ninth buoy is silent.

data.title: Veiled Sister's Sanctum --- Entrance hidden by a mirage that shows your greatest fear.
data.body: The mirage is not an illusion. It is a memory the Sister has stolen. The memory is always from a child.

data.title: Galanina Slave Market --- A circular pit with cages of brass and bone.
data.body: The auctioneer wears a mask. The mask is made from the face of a debt-seller. The face still moves.

data.title: Esoti Record Hall --- A long chamber with shelves of silent scrolls.
data.body: The scrolls write themselves. The ink is the blood of erased names. The ninth shelf is empty --- reserved for the name that must never be recorded.

data.title: Black Hand Garrison --- A nondescript building with no windows and a single door.
data.body: The door has no handle. It opens inward only when a name is whispered. The whisper is never forgotten.

data.title: Breath-less Cellar --- A root cellar with a single candle and a hole in the floor.
data.body: The hole leads to a tunnel that leads to a tomb. The tomb is a safe house. The candle never burns lower.

data.title: Red Desert's Edge --- Where the fertile land turns to dust and glass.
data.body: The glass is green. It hums with the memory of the prince's curse. The sound is the same as a brass cage rattling. [J] The Ninth Name Shrine --- A ruin where a forbidden name is carved into stone. The stone weeps water. The water tastes of iron and forgotten vows. The name is worn smooth --- no one can read it, but everyone fears it. [Q] Spirit-Binding Foundry --- A forge where brass cages are made. The forge is heated by a bound fire-spirit. It screams when the bellows pump. The screams are prayers in a dead language. [K] The Hollow Vessel Nursery --- An orphanage where children are prepared for possession. The children have no shadows. Their shadows have been sold. The ninth cot is always empty --- for the child who will be the Hollow's vessel. [A] Ikasha's Sleeping Chamber --- A sealed vault beneath Galanina. Inside, a stone sarcophagus. The stone is warm. She Who Sleeps dreams of freedom. Her dreams leak through the cracks --- green glass grows where they touch stone. enumerate

data.title: Terrified Baker --- Kneads dough with shaking hands. He knows which Black Hand guards take bribes and which take only silence. He will sell you bread, but he will not meet your eyes. If the Hand asks, he did not see you. He will weep afterward.
data.body: His son was taken for ``reeducation'' last year. He does not know if the boy is alive. He is afraid to ask.

data.title: Ledger Clerk --- Ink-stained fingers, hollow eyes. Copies erasure orders all day. He knows whose names are on next week's list. He will trade that knowledge for a single assurance that his own name isn't on it --- but he cannot be sure you can deliver. He is not brave. He is merely desperate.
data.body: He has a wife and a daughter. The daughter's name is written on a scrap of paper hidden in his shoe. That is his only insurance.

data.title: Black Hand Recruit --- Still has a family. Still flinches when the brand touches his arm. He joined because the mines are a death sentence. He does not know what he will be asked to do next week. He is terrified. He will let you pass if you promise to tell his mother he didn't suffer.
data.body: He has never killed anyone. He does not know if he can.

data.title: Mother at the Well --- Gave her youngest child's name to the Sisters. Not because she is evil. Because the alternative was her whole family being taken. She draws water at dawn when acolytes aren't watching. She will not speak of it. But if you ask about the ninth child, she will weep.
data.body: The child's name was Laila. She hums her daughter's lullaby to the rope. The well remembers.

data.title: Black Hand Veteran --- Has served twenty years. Her hands do not shake. She has seen the Sisters' work up close. She knows there is no escape, only delay. She will not help you escape --- but she might sell you a day's head start. The price is a story. The story must be true.
data.body: She has forgotten the taste of honey. She would like to remember.

data.title: Esoti Junior Magistrate --- Inherited her post from an uncle who disappeared. She knows the laws are lies. She enforces them anyway because the alternative is the Binding Foundry. She drinks too much and weeps in the archive. She has a key to a vault. She will lend it --- for a story about what freedom tastes like.
data.body: The key is a brass finger bone. It fits a lock in the Ninth Ledger's vault. She does not know what it opens.

data.title: Slave --- Not a rebel. Not a hero. Just a woman who has learned to be invisible. She knows the secret passages behind the kitchen. She will trade directions for a single piece of news from outside --- any news, even bad. She wants to know if her village still exists.
data.body: She wears a brass tag with a number. She has memorised the number of every slave in the household. She is waiting for the day the numbers no longer matter.

data.title: Black Hand Officer --- He takes bribes. He looks the other way. He has a daughter in the Sisters' care as a ``ward.'' He knows she is a hostage. He will let you pass if you carry a letter to her --- a letter that says nothing, but is written on paper that smells of home. He is not your ally. He is a man drowning.
data.body: The paper is his daughter's old schoolwork. The ink is his own blood. He does not know if she can still read.

data.title: Veiled Sister --- She was given to the temple at nine. She does not remember her mother. She believes the Veil protects the empire from something worse. She has never seen a slave beaten --- they hide that from novices. She is not evil. She is cultivated. A crack in her certainty may take years to open. You do not have years.
data.body: She wears a veil of hammered silver. Underneath, her face is smooth --- no scars, no wrinkles. She has not aged since she took her vows. [J] The Whisperer (Breath-less cell leader) --- She has three names, each for a different jurisdiction. She moves through the catacombs like smoke. She will trust you only after you have broken a small law in her presence --- not to prove your courage, but to prove you have something to lose. She writes messages on water. The words vanish, but the Sisters cannot read them. Her reflection is missing. She sold it for a name. [Q] The Black Hand's Shadow --- A Hand agent who has stopped sleeping. He sees the Sisters' work in his dreams. He knows he cannot leave. He will not betray his oath --- but he might fail to see you, if the price is a single night of dreamless rest. The price is a memory. He will take the happiest one. He carries a brass bell that rings once every hour. It is the only thing that keeps him awake. He has not heard it ring in three days. [K] The Esoti Censor (Desperate) --- A high-ranking magistrate who has been ordered to falsify a lineage. If she refuses, her family is erased. If she complies, she knows the truth will outlive her. She will give you the original document --- for a promise that her grandson will be told, one day, why his grandmother's name was struck from the rolls. The document is written on human skin. The skin was her own, cut from her thigh when she took office. She has no feeling there anymore. [A] The Veiled Sister (Full) --- Malignant divine justice made flesh. She does not threaten. She does not bargain. She states what will happen. She is always correct. She has never been seen eating, sleeping, or blinking. She is not a woman. She is a function of the Veil. There is no complexity here. There is only the weight of a god's attention. (No debt. No price. Only survival.) Her veil is made of gold coins from a dozen dead empires. They do not clink. They weep when she speaks. enumerate

data.title: Spirit-Dust Storm --- Red sand from the desert carries whispering spirits.
data.body: Navigation DV +1. Mark Fatigue. The voices ask for your name. Do not answer. They already know it.

data.title: Brass Gate Closed --- The strait is sealed for ``inspection.'' Delay 2 segments.
data.body: The ``inspection'' is a hunt for a Breath-less agent. The agent is in your party. The gate knows. The gate is patient.

data.title: Bound Spirit Breaks Free --- A brass cage cracks. The spirit attacks.
data.body: The spirit was once a child. It weeps as it fights. Killing it feels like murder. Freeing it feels like surrender.

data.title: The Veil Fails --- For a moment, the Maeri's magic falters. Spirit-visions haunt all.
data.body: You see the face of someone you wronged. They are asking for an apology. You cannot remember what you did. That is the punishment.

data.title: Black Hand Sweep --- A sudden search of the district. Everyone's papers are checked.
data.body: Your papers are in order. The Black Hand does not care. They take you anyway. The order was the trap.

data.title: Esoti Audit --- A magistrate demands to see your records. Your records are lies.
data.body: The magistrate smiles. ``Everyone lies. I just need to know how much.'' His quill is already moving.

data.title: Spirit-Hound Scent --- A pack of bound hounds is on your trail.
data.body: The hounds are invisible. You can hear their breathing, close and wet. Their breath smells of brass and old prayers.

data.title: Slave Raid --- A Veiled Sister's caravan is taking villagers. You are in the way.
data.body: The villagers are armed. They have been expecting you. You are the bait. The Sister is not here. She is watching.

data.title: Ikasha's Whisper --- In a quiet moment, you hear a voice
data.body: ``Free me.'' The whisper comes from a crack in the floor. A single green eye looks up. The eye is glass. It blinks. [J] The Ninth Name Spoken --- Someone in the party speaks a dead name aloud. The air grows cold. A spirit appears. It wants to know why you called. It does not accept silence as an answer. [Q] Sister's Test --- A Veiled Sister offers a deal: betray a Breath-less contact for safety. The offer is genuine. The price is your soul. The Sister watches you decide. She is not in a hurry. She has all of eternity. [K] Mass Haunting --- The bound spirits rise as one. The Veil is tearing. The spirits do not attack. They simply ask: ``Why did you let this happen?'' They do not mean the empire. They mean the children. [A] The Demon's Weight Called --- The Kalrantha Amulet glows. A voice whispers: ``Speak your desire.'' The whisper is your own. You do not remember giving it permission. The amulet is not a prison. It is a magnet. It draws you toward your fate. enumerate

data.title: Slave's True Name --- Use it to free a bound person --- or bind them further.
data.body: The name is written on a scrap of skin. The skin was the slave's own. The letters are still warm.

data.title: Spirit-Lamp --- Ask one question of a bound spirit. It cannot lie.
data.body: The lamp burns green. The spirit's face appears in the flame. It is weeping. The tears evaporate into glass.

data.title: Brass Seal --- Safe passage in a Sister's sanctum for one visit.
data.body: The seal is warm. It glows when a Sister is lying. It also glows when you are lying. The Sister does not ask which.

data.title: Veil-Clip --- Speak without being silenced by Maeri magic.
data.body: The clip is a small brass spider. It crawls onto your collar and whispers. It whispers the names of those who cannot speak.

data.title: Erased Name Page --- A page from the Esoti record with a name struck through.
data.body: The ink is still wet. The name was erased ten minutes ago. The page is warm. It has a pulse.

data.title: Breath-less Cipher --- A codebook for reading secret messages on water.
data.body: The cipher is written on a leaf. The leaf dissolves when read. The water remembers. The water does not forgive.

data.title: Spirit-Hound Whistle --- Call off a pack of bound hounds once.
data.body: The whistle is made from a child's bone. The child was the hounds' last victim. The hounds remember her scent.

data.title: Ikasha's Dream --- One prophetic vision of the Maeri's next move.
data.body: The dream arrives as a headache. The vision is clear. The cost is one memory. The memory is always of a door closing.

data.title: Black Hand Mask --- Wear it to pass as a Hunter for one scene.
data.body: The mask has no eye holes. The mask sees for you. It also remembers. It will report what it saw to the Hand. [J] Cage-Maker's Flaw --- A key that opens any spirit-cage. One use. The key is a bent nail. It was the flaw the cage-maker left. The flaw is also a prayer. The cage-maker does not know to whom. [Q] Drowned Sister's Secret --- The location of a hidden Breath-less archive. The archive is in a well. The well is guarded by a ghost. The ghost's name is Mercy. She does not remember why. [K] Ninth Sister's Veil --- Wear it to appear as a Veiled Sister for one hour. The veil is also a noose. Do not tie it too tight. The Sister who gave it to you is already dead. She did not untie it. [A] The Unnamed Prince's Map --- A map to the original Kalrantha temple. The map is drawn on human skin. The skin was the prince's own. The map glows under moonlight. It shows the way --- and the cost. enumerate

Cultural Masks The Patrons by Region
The God of Trickery A Special Note
The Inquisitor Prime The Iron Hand of Purity
Lucky Jack The Lord of Thieves
The Unbroken Way The Way of Balance
Longhouse Quarter
data.body: The forum's marble floor is worn smooth by dancing feet, not sandals. The ghosts of tax collectors weep in the corners.

data.title: Milefort XVII
data.body: Earth bank, stone gate; faded eagle over fresh knotwork. The eagle's stone wings were reglued after a lightning strike. It still leans left — toward the steppe.

data.title: Stone Ford
data.body: Plank-palings and a customs table at knee-height; border as bureaucracy. The ford changes hands every season. The customs table never moves. The wood is stained with ink and blood.

data.title: Villa Granary
data.body: Barracks with a tile roof; spear racks where olives once slept. The olive press still works. The pressers are now armorers. The oil is for lamps, not cooking.

data.title: Twin Court
data.body: Mallus ring beneath an oak, basilica bench across the lane. The oak and the bench are the same distance from the well. The well is neutral ground. The well has a chain.

data.title: Blackwood Road
data.body: Milestones re-carved in runes and Utaran both. The runes say “safe passage.” The Utaran says “toll payable twice.” The third line is scratched out.

data.title: Burial Field
data.body: Ship-ridge mounds beside tiled mausolea, both garlanded. The mausolea have fresh offerings. The ancestors are not picky. The ship-mounds whisper at dawn.

data.title: Hill Amphitheater
data.body: A lord's hall raised in an old arena's curve; power in architecture. The lord's throne is a gladiator's chair. He does not know who last sat in it. The sand beneath is still dark.

data.title: New Raivon
data.body: March capital; grid-streets colliding with wandering lanes. The grid was laid by a surveyor who never came back. The lanes are older. They move at night.

data.title: Dux's Palace
data.body: Purple awnings, wolf-hides, law tablets on the wall. The tablets list every treaty broken. The wolf-hides are from the treaty-breakers. They still growl.

data.title: Hearth-Mother Vesna
data.body: Keeper of guest-right. She has never lost a quarrel; her voice is soft, her memory longer than the Foedus Stone. She remembers obligations that are not yet owed—and the stone is forgetting, shrinking.

data.title: March Notary Theodora
data.body: Utaran-trained legalist. Her left hand writes Utaran, her right writes runes. She signs with her foot. A “third hand” writes in ink that no one can read—not even her. The document is always binding—until the stone forgets.

data.title: Horse-Reeve
data.body: Rations pasture between plows and warbands. He measures grass in fistfuls. The Ykrul respect his arithmetic. The Ecktorians pretend not to notice. He is saving fistfuls to patch the stone.

data.title: Ykrul Envoy
data.body: Riding under safe-conduct; speaks obligations in proverbs. He never carries a weapon. His tongue is sharp enough. His hostage string has nine knots. He is running out of space—and the stone is running out of memory.

data.title: Old Legionary
data.body: Drill-master for Vilikari levies; Utar in muscle memory. He still marks time in paces. The recruits call him “Grandfather Eagle.” The eagle on his shield is chipped. He says the stone's cracks are just more places to put his thumb.

data.title: Ecktorial Factor
data.body: Vilikari blood, Ecktorial coin; flows where the market points. His coat has two collars—one for each loyalty. He wears whichever is warmer. His tally has three columns. The third column is labeled “crack width.”

data.title: Kahfagian Pilot
data.body: Lantern-law chit and clan tattoo; sea-law on land. He navigates by stars and tariffs. Both change with the season. He has never been lost—only delayed. The stone's cracks are good for smuggling.

data.title: Marcher-Lord
data.body: Iron-nail crown, Vilikari law in pocket; a frontier king. His crown was a plowshare. He reversed the curse. His hands are still calloused. He does not sit on his throne. He spends his days pressing his ear to the stone.

data.title: Queen of Marches
data.body: Consort-regent; smiles like precedent. She married the Federate King for peace. She kept the kingdom for herself. Her seal is a broken arrow. She keeps a piece of the stone in her pocket—it gets smaller every year.

data.title: Federate King Aldric
data.body: Rex-Dux sworn to forms, sung by his own. He has three thrones—oak, marble, and saddle. He uses whichever is not being argued over. Lately, all three are dusty. He has stopped arguing. He just listens to the stone.

data.title: Elder of Elders
data.body: Thing-council speaker; a nod can unmake a clan. He speaks once a year. The rest of the time he listens—and remembers. But his memory is cracking like the stone. He has started writing things on his own skin.

data.title: Law Tangle
data.body: Mallus verdict vs. basilica writ — whose seal bites? The oak judge and the marble judge are cousins. They send each other holiday cards. The case has been open for three generations. The stone has forgotten who started it.

data.title: Foedus Seal
data.body: Settlement and stipends confirmed for a season. The seal is a bronze wolf's head. It warms when the treaty holds—and cools when it doesn't. The wolf's eyes are garnets. One eye is cracked.

data.title: Mallus Right
data.body: Hold court under the oak and be obeyed. The oak is older than the kingdom. Its roots have seen more verdicts than the throne. The acorns are bitter. The oak's leaves are falling early.

data.title: Stipend Arrears
data.body: Paid in salt and grain; portable, persuasive. The salt is gray. The grain is from last harvest. Both are worth more than coin. The soldiers will accept. The stone will not.

data.title: Utaran Patent
data.body: Citizenship-style privilege; doors open, bows deepen. The patent is a worn scrap of vellum. It has been folded and refolded for a century. The seal is a sunburst. The sunburst is fading.

data.title: Stall-Right
data.body: Customs favor on a frontier market line. The stall is a painted plank. Plant it, and the tax man will pretend not to see you. He will remember the favor. The stone will not.

data.title: Remount Allotment
data.body: Fresh horses from royal paddocks, no questions. The horses are from the king's own herd. They know the roads better than you. They also know the king's secrets. They refuse to cross the stone's shadow.

data.title: Bridge Farm
data.body: Imperial for a season; funds and friends accrue. The bridge toll is a copper a head. The bridge keeper is your new best friend. He also keeps a list of your enemies. He scratches the list on the stone.

data.title: Purple Warrant
data.body: Wear the stripe; officials defer on sight. The stripe is a sash. It was a curtain in a past life. The present life is yours. Do not lose it. The stone's crack has swallowed one like it.

data.title: Queen's Audience
data.body: Private; a whisper becomes policy. The audience is held in a garden. The flowers are listening. The gardener is a spy. The gardener is also the queen. She keeps a piece of the stone under her tongue.

data.title: Dux Commission
data.body: Command a mixed unit with pay authority. The commission is a baton. It doubles as a mace in a pinch. It also doubles as a receipt. The receipt is overdue. The stone has a receipt for the stone.

data.title: Wolf Milepost
data.body: Stacked stones; wind whines through eye-holes. Each stone is a tally. Remove one, and the wind names you debtor.

data.title: Remount Station
data.body: Low corral with stamped snow and tether-posts. The tether-posts are carved with the names of dead horses. The living ones remember.

data.title: Birch Windbreak
data.body: Above black-earth tracks; old offerings in the bark. The offerings are strips of wool. Each strip is a prayer for safe crossing.

data.title: Salt Pan
data.body: Crusted white; hoof-prints like stars across the void. The pan has a name: “The Khagan's Mirror.” Look into it, and you see what you owe.

data.title: Reed Ford
data.body: River braids; poles mark yesterday's safe line. The poles shift in the night. The river's path changes with the moon.

data.title: Trading Palisade
data.body: Way-post with wolf-skull pennons snapping. The skulls face outward. They watch for liars and bad weights.

data.title: Winter Camp
data.body: Felt tents in a horseshoe facing the wind. The open end is for guests. The closed end is for the ancestors.

data.title: Kurgan Field
data.body: Low barrows; horse-bones bead the grass like prayer beads. The bones were placed by a bone-singer. Each bead is a name.

data.title: Watch Kopje
data.body: Lonely tor with signal fire-scar; the eye of the steppe. The fire-scar is from a signal that saved a host. The smoke still smells of hope.

data.title: Pontoon Crossing
data.body: Laced hides creak; the current speaks fast and hungry. The hides are from horses that died crossing. Their ghosts still pull.

data.title: Council Hollow
data.body: Standards planted; the ground tamped like a war-drum. The standards have ears. Speak a treason here, and every clan will know by dawn.

data.title: Khagan's Station
data.body: Broad ger on a timber platform; guards in silence. The guards never blink. They are paid in salt and secrets.

data.title: Sky Steppe
data.body: Open, wind like a voice; tracks keep pace beside you. The tracks are not yours. They belong to the ancestors who ride with you.

data.title: Herd-Scout
data.body: Three ponies and six opinions; the horizon as a map. He can read a trail by the way the grass bends. He can read a liar by the way a rider checks his exits.

data.title: Camp-Mother
data.body: Chooses where fires live; hospitality is law. She has never drawn a blade. She has never needed to.

data.title: Banner Youth
data.body: Minding the wolves' tooth standard; pride as duty. The standard is older than his grandmother's grandmother. He will die before it falls.

data.title: Salt-Broker
data.body: Weighs promises like grain; trade as precision. Her scales are honest—because a dishonest scale is a broken tool, and tools are expensive.

data.title: Remount Keeper
data.body: String-master with a book of brands; horses as currency. His book is written in hoof-prints. He can read a horse's soul.

data.title: Bone-Singer
data.body: Knows the kurgans' proper names; death as memory. She sings the names of the dead each dawn. The dead sing back.

data.title: Road-Judge
data.body: Tümen scribe with seals and a patient ear. His seals are from three empires. He uses whichever one is still valid.

data.title: Noyan Envoy
data.body: Silver paiza, iron smile; diplomacy as a blade. His paiza was a gift from a Khagan who is now dead. He does not mention that.

data.title: Host Captain
data.body: The tent-wall is a map; strategy in every fold. He can see a battle in the way smoke rises. He is usually right.

data.title: Falcon Courier
data.body: Leather gauntlets, answers sooner than asked. The falcon is a sleeper agent. It belongs to a different clan. The courier doesn't know.

data.title: Khatun of Ring
data.body: Keeper of camp-law and hostage strings. Her strings are braided from the hair of hostages. She knows each strand's owner.

data.title: Khagan's Kin
data.body: A nephew or niece sent to bind a foedus with a look. They have never lost a negotiation. They have never needed to speak.

data.title: Sky-Speaker
data.body: Shaman of storms; shortcuts owe them a price. They can call lightning—or call it off. The price is always a story.

data.title: White Squall
data.body: Dry snow, lost horizons; navigation by gut and horse sense. The snow tastes of iron. Someone is bleeding nearby.

data.title: Rasputitsa
data.body: The road becomes porridge; wheels are lies on the earth. The mud has a smell—old blood and older lies.

data.title: Remount Sickness
data.body: A cough in the string; swaps get awkward, trust thinner. The cough is a curse. The horses know who cast it.

data.title: Salt Shortage
data.body: Meat spoils; tempers thin like winter air. The salt was cut with grave dust. Someone wanted the winter to be hard.

data.title: Hostage Call
data.body: Protocol invoked; someone must sit in the tent. The tent has no floor. The hostage can see the earth beneath—and the bones.

data.title: Feud Spark
data.body: A name spoken wrong reopens an old debt; blood is the only coin that pays. The name was spelled correctly. The insult was in the pause before it.

data.title: Grassfire
data.body: Runs with the wind faster than horses; escape as a prayer. The fire has a face. It is the face of a Khagan who burned a village.

data.title: Foedus Recall
data.body: Treaty terms re-read; your papers disagree. The treaty was written on both sides. The other side used a different ink.

data.title: River Break
data.body: Ice goes; ferries don't; crossing becomes a gamble. The ice is still thick in the middle. The edges are lying.

data.title: Raid Shadow
data.body: Another banner follows at a patient distance. They are not attacking. They are waiting for you to make a mistake.

data.title: Kurultai Call
data.body: Camps converge; travel becomes politics. The kurultai has a list of grievances. Your name is near the top.

data.title: Wolf Muster
data.body: A levy raised; every road a checkpoint, every rider a judge. The muster horn is a wolf's skull. It sounds like a scream.

data.title: Sky Omen
data.body: Three suns, or none; routes rewrite themselves. The omen is a wedge of cranes flying north in winter. The sky is wrong.

data.title: Camp Token
data.body: One night's lawful fire and fodder; hospitality as a right. The token is a horsehair braid. Burn it to claim your fire.

data.title: Salt Allotment
data.body: Draw from a named store without quarrel. The allotment is a salt-cake. Break it in half to share.

data.title: Ford-Right
data.body: Cross a named braid at lawful depth. The right is a pole. Plant it in the river, and the ford will hold—once.

data.title: Remount Chit
data.body: Swap two tired mounts for fresh. The chit is a horse's tooth. The remount keeper will not smile when you present it.

data.title: Escort Braid
data.body: Two riders see you through a bad stretch. The braid is woven from the riders' own hair. They will die before they cut it.

data.title: Safe-Hostage
data.body: Place or take token-kin for a truce. The hostage is a child. The child is patient.

data.title: Paiza Tablet
data.body: Priority on the Wolf Road and at posts. The tablet is bronze. It is warm when your reputation is good.

data.title: Market-Green
data.body: Trade under a banner; weapons sheathed. The banner is a green field. No blood may be spilled beneath it.

data.title: Standard Guard
data.body: Travel under wolf-tooth; raiders defer. The standard is a wolf's tooth on a pole. Raiders will bow—or die.

data.title: Ring Audience
data.body: The Khatun hears you alone; precedent sticks. The audience is held at midnight. The fire is the only witness.

data.title: Khagan's Writ
data.body: Doors open, mouths close across the steppe. The writ is a sheet of hammered silver. It bends, but it does not break.

data.title: Sky's Exception
data.body: Once, the weather ignores you (storm, whiteout, dust). The exception is a single breath. Use it well.
